Umesh M Adiga J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This is claimant's appeal against judgment and award passed by the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal and III Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ramanagara (hereinafter for short referred to as "Tribunal") in M.V.C.No.492 of 2017 dated 29.10.2021 claiming for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Ramanagara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. This case was slated for hearing on admission and with the consent of the learned Advocates appearing NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB for both side parties, the matter was taken up for final disposal.
3. We refer to the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal.
4. It is the case of claimants that on 12.09.2017 at about 7.30 pm, deceased Jayalakshmamma was waiting for a bus near Milk Dairy of Shyanubhoganahalli, Ramanagara Taluk.

She met with an Rangappa vs Keerthi on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149217590/
2 accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Autorickshaw bearing Registration No.KA-42-A-5029 by its driver.
Due to impact of the accident, she had sustained severe head injuries.
She was taken to Ramakrishna Hospital of Ramanagara wherein she succumbed to the injuries.
It is further case of the claimants that deceased was aged about 49 years at the time of accident.
She was vending milk and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and contributing the said income to the maintenance of the family.

The claimants, being husband and daughter of the NC:
2023:KHC:41713-DB deceased were depending on her income.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.25 lakhs.
5. Both the respondents had appeared before the Tribunal and filed their respective written statements.

Respondent No.1 had denied contentions of claimants in the claim petition and had further stated that the said vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2 and in the event, if the compensation is awarded, then Respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify him and pay the compensation.

6. The Respondent No.2 had also denied all the contents of the claim petition and it had further stated that its liability is restricted to terms and conditions of policy of insurance and holding of valid and effective driving license by the driver of the said Autorickshaw.
With these reasons, they prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
7. The Tribunal, on the basis of rival contentions of the parties, had framed necessary issues for consideration.
The claimants, to prove their case, examined PW-1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P7.
The Respondents have examined RWs-1 and 2 and got marked Exs.R1 to R3.
It appears, evidence of RW-2 is incomplete.

9. The Tribunal, after hearing the arguments and on appreciating of pleadings and evidence of both the parties, partly allowed the claim petition awarding following amount of compensation:
SL.NO. HEADS OF COMPENSATION AMOUNT OF COMPENSATION (IN RUPEES)
1. Loss of dependency 5,46,000 (Rs.3,500x12x13)
2. Loss of estate 15,000 3.
Loss of consortium 40,000 4.

Funeral expenses 15,000 Rangappa vs Keerthi on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149217590/
3 5.
Transportation of dead body 5,000 and conveyance Total 6,21,000 10.
The Tribunal held that the owner of the Autorickshaw had violated terms and conditions of policy of insurance and driver of the said Autorickshaw had no valid and effective driving license.
Therefore, directed NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation and recover the same from owner of the vehicle.

The Tribunal assessed income of deceased as Rs.7,000/- per month; her age as 49 years; and multiplier applicable to the case in hand was '13',
deducted 50% of her income towards personal expenses and calculated the compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'.
11.

We have heard the arguments of the learned Advocate for appellant and Respondent No.2.
12.

The learned Advocate for Appellant would submit that the Tribunal had not taken income of deceased properly and the Tribunal had taken the notional income of the deceased as Rs.7,000/- per month, which is on lower side.
He further submits that even while settlement of the dispute before the Lok-Adalath, income of a victim of an accident of the year 2017 is considered as Rs.11,000/- per month.
Atleast, the Tribunal ought to have applied the same to the case in hand.
However, the Tribunal failed to consider the same.
He further submits that the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB had not added future prospects to the earnings of the deceased.
The deceased was married lady and claimant No.1 is her husband.
Inspite of that, the Tribunal has deducted 50% of her income towards personal expenses, which is erroneous.
Since she was a married lady, one- third of her income ought to be deducted towards personal expenses.
He further submitted that amount of compensation awarded under other heads are also meagre and hence, prayed to enhance the amount of compensation.

13. The learned Advocate for Respondent No.2/ Insurer has vehemently contended that deceased was the wife of claimant No.1 and claimants failed to prove that she was an agriculturist or she was a milk vendor and she had any source of income to contribute to the family.
Moreover, claimant No.1 is husband of the deceased and claimant No.2 is major daughter of the deceased.
According to her evidence, she has daughter aged about 16 years.

Therefore, both the claimants are not NC:
2023:KHC:41713-DB dependants on earnings of the deceased.
When the claimants are not dependants, the income has to be calculated in a different formula and the formula applied by the Tribunal is not in accordance with the law.

The learned counsel has further submitted that the Tribunal, however, rightly deducted 50% of her income towards personal expenses, which is proper,
and he submits that the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and prayed for dismissing the appeal.
14. The Tribunal had appreciated evidence on record and rightly held that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw by its driver.
The said fact is not disputed and Respondent/Insurer has not challenged the said findings.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere in the said findings.
15. The claimants are husband and daughter of deceased Jayalakshmamma, is also not in dispute.

It is also an admitted fact that she died in a vehicle accident by involvement of Autorickshaw bearing Rangappa vs Keerthi on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149217590/
4 Registration No.KA- NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB 42-A-5029.
The claimants are legal heirs of the deceased.
Therefore, they are entitled to file the claim petition to claim the compensation for death of Smt.Jayalakshmamma.
The claimants had contended that deceased was an agriculturist and milk vendor and used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
They were unable to prove the said fact before the Tribunal.

Therefore,
Tribunal has assessed the notional income of deceased as Rs.7,000/- per month.
The said assessment of income of claimant is on lower side.

Normally, in case of settlement of motor vehicle claim petitions before the Lok-Adalath, notional income of a victim of an accident of the year 2017,
is considered as Rs.11,000/- per month and same could be applied to the facts of the present case.

16. In the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs.
PRANAY - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB SETHI AND OTHERS1 the Hon'ble Apex Court held that future prospects of a victim of an accident has to be considered while awarding the compensation.

entities.text:
NATIONAL INSURANCE NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs.
PRANAY - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB SETHI AND OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, in this case, age of the deceased was 49 years.
As per above said judgment between age group of 40 to 50 years, 25% of income has to be added to income towards future prospects.
Much controversy is, in respect of deductions of the amount towards personal expenses.

According to submission of learned Advocate for Appellant, one-third of her income ought to be deducted by the Tribunal towards personal expenses since deceased was married lady and it is the contention of Insurer that claimants were not depending upon income of the deceased; Claimant No.2 is major and married daughter and she has a daughter of 16 years old as on the date of her evidence.
Therefore, she cannot be considered as dependent on the earnings of the deceased.
Considering these facts, the Tribunal had 2017 ACJ 2700 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB deducted 50% of income towards personal expenses and it does not call for interference.
17. It is settled principle of law that if a married person dies in a motor vehicle accident, then one-third of his/her income has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
In the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra) as well as SARLA VERMA Vs. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION2, the Hon'ble Apex Court held above said principle.

entities.text: SARLA VERMA Vs. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case of Sarla Verma (referred supra) it is held that:
"In order to arrive at the contribution to the dependants, the personal and living expenses of the deceased should be deducted from his/her income.
But no evidence need to be lead to show the actual expenses of the deceased.

Infact, any evidence in Rangappa vs Keerthi on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149217590/
5
that behalf will be wholly unverifiable and likely to be unreliable.
The claimants will obviously tend to claim that deceased was very frugal and did not have any expensive habits and was spending virtually the entire income on the family.

On the other hand,
it will be difficult for the respondents in (2009) 6 SCC 121 - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB claim petitions to produce evidence to show that deceased was spending a considerable part of the income on himself or that he was contributing only a small part of income on his family.
Therefore, it becomes necessary to standardize the deductions to be made and under the head of personal and living expenses of the deceased to stop.

This lead to the practice of deducting towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, one-third of the income if the deceased was married, and one-half (50%) of the income if the deceased was a bachelor.
This practice was evolved out of experience, logic and convenience.
In fact, one-third deductions got statutory recognition under the second schedule to the Motor Vehicles Act 1988, in respect of claims under Section 163-A of the said Act.
But, such percentage of deductions is not an inflexible rule and offers merely a guidelines.

Though in some cases the deduction to be made towards personal and living expenses is calculated on the basis of units indicated in the U.P.STATE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS Vs. TRILOK CHANDRA AND OTHERS3, the general practice is to apply standardized deductions having considered several subsequent decisions of the Supreme Court, it is opined that (1996) 4 SCC 362 - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, should be one-third, where the number of dependent family members is two to three, one- fourth, where the number of dependent family members is four to six,
and one-fifth, where the number of dependent family members exceeds six.

entities.text: U.P.STATE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS Vs. TRILOK CHANDRA AND OTHERS3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But where the deceased was a bachelor, and the claimants are the parents, the deduction follows a different principle.
In regard to bachelors, normally, 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.
Even otherwise, there is also the possibility of his getting married in a short time, in which event, the contribution to the parents and siblings is likely to be cut drastically.
Further, subject to evidence to the contrary, the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependent and the mother alone will be considered as a dependent.
In the absence of evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters will not be considered as dependents because they will be either independent and earning, or married, or be dependent on the father.

Thus, even if the deceased is survived by parents and siblings, only the mother would be considered to be a dependent, and 50% would be treated as the personal and - 14 - Rangappa vs Keerthi on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149217590/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB living expenses of the bachelor and 50% as the contribution to the family.
However, where the family of a bachelor is large and dependent on the income of the deceased, as in a case where he has a widowed mother and a large number of younger non-earning sisters or brothers, his personal and living expenses may be restricted to one-third and contribution to the family will be taken as two- third."
18.
In the above said land-mark judgment in the case of SARLA VERMA (referred supra), there are two classifications; one is, married and another is unmarried.
It does not make any difference between death of husband or wife.

In this case, it was the contention of the claimants that deceased was an agriculturist and milk vendor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and contributing the said income for the maintenance of the family.
19. In the cross-examination of PW-1, it was not brought out by the respondents that husband of deceased had lucrative source of income.
Normally, in the villages, each and every member of family would go for work to meet family expenses since earning from agriculture or agriculture labour is less.

If they had agricultural lands, they will cultivate or work in their own lands and if they do not have any agricultural lands, then, they will go to work in another's land as coolie and earn for maintenance of the family and normally such earnings would be contributed for the maintenance of the family.
There is no cross-examination in this regard to PW-1.

Under such circumstances, it is difficult to accept the contention of the learned advocate for the Respondent/Insurer that more amount of income should be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased since the claimants were not dependant upon her earnings.
20. For the sake of discussion, even if we accept that deceased was homemaker, then also, her services to the family needs to be considered.
She serves the family in various facets.

She lives as a wife to her husband,
- 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB mother to her children, and she had emotional attachment with the members of the family.
Merely claimant No.2 is a married daughter or residing in her husband's house cannot be considered that there is no emotional attachment of claimant No.2 with her mother.
Her service to the family cannot be valued in terms of the money.
Such benefit has been lost by both the claimants due to death of Smt.Jayalakshmamma.
The said service cannot be substituted.
Under these circumstances, the submission of learned Advocate for Respondent No.2 is not accepted and one-third of income of the deceased is deducted towards personal expenses.
It is not in dispute that the multiplier applicable to the facts of the present case is '13'.

Therefore, the compensation to be assessed under the head loss of dependency is:
 Income of Rs.11,000/-
Rangappa vs Keerthi on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149217590/
7  deceased per  month  Add 25% of Rs.2,750/-
future prospects

- 17 -  NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB  Total Rs.13,750/-
 Less 1/3rd  towards personal  expenses Rs.4,583/-
 Total Rs.9,167/-
Rs.9,167X12X13 = Rs.14,30,052/-.

Compensation needs to be awarded under conventional heads on the basis of law laid down in PRANAY SETHI's case (referred supra) and SHRI RAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. BHAGAT SINGH RAWAT & ORS4,
21.

entities.text: SHRI RAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. BHAGAT SINGH RAWAT & ORS4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal, by following the law laid down in the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra) has awarded the compensation under the conventional heads.
It is also observed in the above said case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra) that after every three years, 10% the said of income has to be enhanced in the above said conventional heads.
Accordingly, the compensation needs to be enhanced.

For the aforesaid discussion, claimants are entitled for following amount of compensation:
 Sl.No. Particulars Amount (Rs.)
 1 Loss of dependency 14,30,052
2 Loss
of consortium 48,700

3 Loss of estate 18,150  4 Funeral expenses 18,150  TOTAL 15,15,052 Rangappa vs Keerthi on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149217590/
8  Claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.8,94,052/-.
23.
The Tribunal, appreciating the evidence on record held that Respondent No.1/Owner of Autorickshaw had violated terms and conditions of policy of insurance.
According to the evidence of RW-1, the said vehicle was plying in area wherein he had no permit and the driver of the said Autorickshaw had no valid and effective driving license.
Therefore, the claimants have violated terms and conditions of policy of insurance.
Moreover, claimants are third parties.

Therefore, as per the settled principles of law, the Insurer has to pay the said amount of - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:41713-DB compensation and can recover it from the Respondent No.1.
24.

For the aforesaid discussion, we pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
c) Apportionment, deposit and release of the amount are as ordered by the Tribunal.
